paper_title: Memorization and Knowledge Injection in Gated LLMs
caption: Analysis on the embedding quality in Llama intermediate layers. Correct gate rate is computed as the rate of question embeddings which have the maximum inner product with the relevant passage embedding. It is computed for each dataset partition, which has 50 passage samples. Shaded area is the standard deviation across 20 dataset partitions. We found that embeddings at the input of MLP layers are better than at the input of attention layers. We choose to use last MLP layer input as embedding in the main experiments of MEGa.

annotations.annotation: The line plot illustrates the average correct gate rate across different embedding layers. The x-axis is labeled "Embedding Layer" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 35, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis represents the "Average Correct Gate Rate", also using a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The plot features four lines: a solid blue line representing "Character Attention input", a dashed blue line for "Character MLP input", a solid red line for "Wiki Attention input", and a dashed red line for "Wiki MLP input". The solid blue line starts at approximately 0.1, rises to a peak near 0.8 around layer 5, declines towards layer 15 to 0.3, and then recovers slightly towards the end and finishes at approximately 0.7. The dashed blue line starts just above 0.82, peaks around 0.9 at layer 3, decreases towards layer 12, and maintains between 0.8 and 0.9 towards layer 30. The solid red line begins approximately at 0.2, peaks around 0.8 at layer 5, dips significantly around layer 15, and then increases to approximately 0.7 towards the end. The dashed red line starts slightly above 0.8, reaches just over 0.85 by layer 5, shows a decline around layer 15, and concludes around 0.85 towards layer 30. Both blue and red shaded regions indicate variability around each corresponding line. The two solid lines closely follow each other and intersect at multiple points, as for the two dashed lines. There is a legend box on the bottom right of the plot to map different marker styles to their labels.
